question: In an obtuse-angled triangle ABC, the length of its longest side AB is 50 cm and one of the other two sides is 42 cm. If the area of the triangle is 294 cm2 , what is the length (in cm) of its third side?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height (h) of the triangle with base 42 cm = (2 × Area) ÷ Base = (2 × 294) ÷ 42 = 14 cm.

In right ΔABD (where D is the projection of B on base line AC), AD = √(50² − 14²) = √(2500 − 196) = 48 cm.

Since the triangle is obtuse and AB is the longest side, vertex C lies between A and D.

Distance CD = AD − AC = 48 − 42 = 6 cm.

Third side BC = √(BD² + CD²) = √(14² + 6²) = √(196 + 36) = √232 = 2√58 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 2√58 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Longest side (c) = AB = 50 cm

Side (b) = AC = 42 cm

Area = 294 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Area of triangle = 1/2 × base × height

Pythagoras Theorem: Side² = Height² + Base²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let AC be the base. Area = 1/2 × AC × h

⇒ 294 = 1/2 × 42 × h

⇒ h = 294 ÷ 21 = 14 cm (Height BD)

⇒ In right-angled ΔABD, AD² + BD² = AB²

⇒ AD² + 14² = 50²

⇒ AD² = 2500 − 196 = 2304

⇒ AD = √2304 = 48 cm

⇒ Since ΔABC is obtuse at C, D lies outside AC. CD = AD − AC

⇒ CD = 48 − 42 = 6 cm

⇒ In right-angled ΔBCD, BC² = BD² + CD²

⇒ BC² = 14² + 6² = 196 + 36 = 232

⇒ BC = √232 = √(4 × 58) = 2√58 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2√58 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Obtuse Triangle Condition

For a triangle with sides a, b, and longest side c, it is obtuse if c² > a² + b².

Area of Triangle (Heron's Formula)

Area = √(s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)), where s = (a+b+c)/2 is the semi-perimeter.

Cosine Rule

For any triangle, c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos(C). If C > 90°, cos(C) is negative, making c² > a² + b².</p
